investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient allocatable capacity (all VM slots occupied or at limit), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~141–145 seconds across all three sibling checks before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence output and a full contract-gap failure. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient allocatable capacity (all VM slots occupied or at limit), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~141–145 seconds across all three sibling checks before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence output and a full contract-gap failure. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata/PeerPods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-05 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting zero available nodes: 2 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval pod for remote-agent-runtime was stuck unscheduled for 145 seconds before timing out, producing no evidence output and failing every required-evidence assertion in the contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) could not schedule the eval probe pod because the two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource were fully saturated (0 of 2 had capacity), and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. Because the pod never became Running, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1918) never completed, no agent was provisioned, and the eval returned empty evidence — failing all five required-evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) and the message assertion ("hello from aura"). This is an eval infrastructure failure caused by a Kubernetes resource/scheduling constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots on the kata/peerpods-capable nodes were consumed by other workloads at the time of the eval run, leaving no capacity for the probe pod.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent probe pod requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata/peerpods nodes carry; those 4 nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of capacity.

TERTIARY — cluster under-provisioning: the production-api cluster has only 2 nodes capable of running kata.peerpods.io/vm workloads; if concurrent remote-agent workloads (real or eval) are scheduled simultaneously, capacity can be exhausted transiently.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — eval scheduling overlap: all three sibling checks ran sequentially within ~5 minutes (remote-agent-create ended 15:41, remote-agent-state ended 15:43, remote-agent-runtime ended 15:46); if each probe pod held VM slots while waiting, they may have competed with each other or with production pods for the same limited resource.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed ample kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity (e.g., several free slots) at the time of the eval run, resource exhaustion would not be the cause and a misconfigured pod spec or admission webhook would need investigation.

If the pod spec for the remote-agent probe did not actually request kata.peerpods.io/vm resources, the 'Insufficient' message would point to a cluster-level misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeded without any cluster changes, the failure was a transient capacity spike rather than a sustained exhaustion condition.

If the 4 nodes that failed the affinity check were recently relabeled or had their taints changed, the affinity mismatch could be a configuration regression rather than an expected topology constraint.

If no other workloads were consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the time of the failure, the 2 eligible nodes may have a lower-than-expected VM limit configured, pointing to a node configuration issue rather than workload contention.
